A circular orbit that is off-center has a center of perihelion that lies at an angle to the body it orbits, which could be a sun-like object. This type of orbit results in a unique radiation pattern, characterized by a modulation of intensity and frequency. The pattern can be visualized as a circle within a circle, with the inner circle rotating at a different speed than the outer one. This phenomenon can be observed in a binary system consisting of two sun-like objects. The radiation pattern can be detected and analyzed, and our research suggests that it could be used to study compact binary systems.
We examine the existence and uniqueness of solutions to a non-local equation on a compact surface, specifically focusing on generalizations of the Minkowski problem and the Brascamp-Lieb inequality.

This paper presents an innovative method for tracking and locating multiple
objects in a surveillance area. The proposed approach relies on a Monte Carlo
framework to generate multiple scenarios, from which the most probable trajectory
for an object can be determined. In contrast to existing methods, which rely on
forward simulation, our method employs backward simulation to identify the most
probable object trajectory. Our novel algorithm efficiently handles a large number
of objects and their corresponding trajectories, and we demonstrate its effectiveness
by comparing it to a Monte Carlo algorithm and a deterministic optimization method
on both simulated and real-world data.

This study examines the stability of multi-feed control strategies implemented in power electronic systems, which are represented by admittance matrices. To assess stability, a linearized model of the multi-feed control system is analyzed using the Lyapunov matrix, under the assumption that the power network's admittance matrix is diagonalized. The results show that the stability of the multi-feed control system is influenced by the power network's eigenvalues, and that the Lyapunov matrix provides a measure of the control system's stability. The findings are validated through simulations of a power grid connected to multiple control systems, which confirm the analytical predictions.

This study examines the distinctiveness and stability of online signature signatures, considering both time-based and session-based verification methods.
We investigate the time-based approach, where a user's signature signature remains unchanged over time and sessions, by analyzing its components, including dynamic and static traits, as well as the features of the signature area and writing patterns.
We evaluate the distinctiveness of the signature signature using various distances, such as Euclidean and Dynamic Time Warping, and the consistency of the verification process with the one-vs-all and one-vs-one metrics, using a large dataset of 1,200 users from a real-world signing verification system.
We also assess the ease of re-creation of the signature signature using a generative model based on the features extracted from the training data, and the results indicate that the signature signature exhibits moderate distinctiveness and stability, but is relatively easy to re-create.

The representations of $h_n(k)$ and $h_{n,r}(k)$ as volumes of certain polytopes are provided, with a specific connection to the volume of a particular arrangement of shifted copies of the $k$-dimensional cross-polytope.

A key advantage of concurrent programming is the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously, thereby improving overall efficiency. However, real-world applications often involve complex, dynamic environments that current concurrent models fail to account for effectively. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that treats persistent environmental factors as shared memory resources accessible by individual processes. We demonstrate that this framework enables the creation of robust, reliable, and predictable concurrent systems even in complex scenarios where environmental dynamics are unpredictable.

This study introduces a novel neural network architecture that enhances 3D human pose estimation from videos, incorporating a 2D pose transform layer to leverage existing 2D pose estimation techniques. The proposed network utilizes an attention mechanism to identify relevant frames and an encoder-decoder architecture to reconstruct the 3D pose, with dilated convolutions enabling the extraction of features from distant temporal areas. The network's performance is evaluated on the CMU MoBo dataset, demonstrating that it surpasses previous methods with a significant improvement in accuracy.

The Cadmium Zinc Telluride (CZT) detector, used in the AstroSat's Cadmium Zinc Telluride Spectro-Polarimetry instrument, is a hard X-ray detector with a unique characteristic of being able to measure all directions. This makes it an ideal instrument for monitoring transient events and locating sources. This article focuses on utilizing CZT in an all-sky mode, specifically through the Earth Occultation Technique, to identify transient X-ray sources. The article presents a method to locate sources using occultation data and provides an example of its effectiveness in locating a recently discovered transient X-ray source, 1RXS J140233.26-292103.4.

This paper presents a novel framework for analyzing the efficiency of blockchain protocols, grounded in the principles of asymptotic efficiency, consensus theory, and potential theory. The proposed framework is applied to the consensus and agreement problems, and its implications are further examined in the context of traditional blockchain protocols, such as PBFT and HotStuff, as well as novel approaches like leaderless protocols and byzantine consensus solutions. The analysis yields a deeper understanding of these protocols' characteristics and provides a basis for comparing their efficiency.

In this research, we calculated the mass spectra of doubly heavy tetraquarks (cc\bar{c}\bar{b}) and (bb\bar{c}\bar{c}), using a model with an enhanced chromomagnetic interaction. The calculated mass spectra for the tetraquark states, including both spin-singlet and spin-triplet, showed a strong correlation with the experimental data on the recently discovered doubly charmed states $X_{cc}^{++}$ and $X_{cc}^{0}$. This led us to predict the existence of the doubly bottom tetraquark state, which we found to be approximately 20.1 GeV/c$^2$ in mass.

We investigate the electroweak vacuum instability in a theory that includes a Higgs doublet and multiple scalar singlets, where the singlets have a weak connection to the Standard Model through gauge symmetry. We find that the singlets' mass values are constrained by the strength of this connection and the degree of instability, with stronger and more extreme instability requiring lighter, non-accessible scalar masses. The singlets' interaction with the Higgs can also be used to explain why the Standard Model has a single charge, by addressing the issue of double charge. The theory naturally generates a gauge charge hierarchy, with the non-standard charges being significantly smaller than the standard charge. We also discuss the potential for these new charges to be detected at the Large Hadron Collider.
We prove the $q$-Logarithmic Sobolev and $p$-Talagrand inequalities in the context of Carnot groups, with $1\leq q\leq\infty$ and $1\leq p\leq\infty$.

We explore the minimal Bregman divergence estimator in the context of a parametric exponential model, demonstrating that a natural, unbiased, and consistent estimator reaches its minimum divergence value when the natural parameter equals the maximum likelihood estimate. This is further supported by numerical simulations and real-data analysis, with algorithmic implementation and public domain release provided in the appendix for reference.

We introduce a novel method for generating high-quality, novel views of real-world dynamic scenes from a limited amount of sparse monocular data. Our approach leverages a NeRF model, incorporating a novel loss function that enables the capture of dynamic scenes with intricate motion patterns. The proposed method excels in its ability to handle scenes with complex motion, intricate geometry, and fine details, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in comprehensive benchmarks and a new, dynamic scene dataset.

A specific property of quantum graphs known as the "spectral form factor" has been studied in the context of random matrix theory, particularly when the semiclassical limit is applied. This work explores an alternative approach to analyze a related characteristic of quantum graphs without relying on the semiclassical limit. A notable correlation is observed between the investigated quantity and the Poissonian expectation, with the distinction between the two providing insight into the graph's spectral properties. This analysis is grounded in the principles of periodic orbit theory.

A novel approach has been developed for estimating the orbital periods of periodic variable stars. This method utilizes a two-dimensional grid search to pinpoint the optimal orbital period and amplitude of these variables. The method's efficacy has been demonstrated through the analysis of OGLE-20131019, a specific type of RR Lyrae star, thereby confirming its potential for determining the orbital parameters of periodic variable stars.

A negative imaginary framework is a foundational concept for designing stabilizing controllers of passive systems with negative real axis dynamics. This paper introduces an approach to transform any given plant model into a nearest negative imaginary framework, which has practical applications in controller design. This transformation is achieved by minimizing the distance between the plant and a negative imaginary system in the Euclidean or Frobenius norm. The paper also explores the design of controllers for negative imaginary systems and demonstrates that they can effectively stabilize plant models that deviate from these systems.

In the context of lifelong machine learning, we investigate methods for continually expanding the capabilities of an automatic speech recognition system that operates in a single language. By utilizing a pre-trained neural network and fine-tuning it on new data, we demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in adapting to shifting performance standards without compromising on previous achievements. This technique is particularly relevant to developing and deploying continuous improvements to existing systems. We evaluate the proposed method using a large dataset of transcribed speech and a smaller dataset of less common speech patterns. By doing so, we achieve state-of-the-art accuracy while outperforming the current best results by a margin of 10% on the smaller dataset. Furthermore, we observe that incorporating the larger dataset into the training process leads to a significant improvement in performance on the smaller dataset.

This research paper details our submission to the 2020 NLP Challenge: Sentiment Analysis in Code-Switching Language, with a two-stream deep learning model that leverages pre-trained BERT for improved performance. We achieved a ranking of #12 among 37 participating teams.

We present a theoretical framework for a three-loop seesaw mechanism that is connected to leptogenesis and dark matter creation. The model is characterized by the presence of a right-handed neutrino, a pair of Higgs doublets, a Higgs singlet, and two dark matter fermions. The singlet's connection to the Standard Model is established through a $Z_3$ symmetry, leading to a radiative seesaw mechanism. The model's predictive power is demonstrated by the calculation of the neutrino mass matrix's eigenvalues, showing that its vacuum expectation values are highly constrained by the observed neutrino data. The model's thermal leptogenesis is also studied, with results indicating that its parameters are consistent with various conditions for successful leptogenesis. The model's stability is further confirmed by the calculation of the dark matter fermions' mass and life expectancy, showing that they can form stable, long-lived particles that are consistent with current experimental data.

Recent advancements in neural networks for handling categorical data have been applied to language processing tasks, but their potential for addressing structured data remains unexplored. This study leverages these findings to propose a novel approach for user response prediction, a task within the computer-mediated communication framework. By combining neural networks for categorical data, our model learns and represents items in a continuous, high-dimensional space. This representation is then integrated into an LSTM architecture, which utilizes it to generate the most likely subsequent utterances. Experimental results on two datasets from the CMC domain demonstrate the superior performance of our model compared to existing approaches.

This research focuses on developing a cell-free network with an intelligent reflecting surface that can provide reliable communication. The system's design involves jointly optimizing the placement of base stations, placement of IRSs, resource allocation, and phase shift adjustments. The phase shift adjustments are constrained by the physical limitations of IRSs and are formulated as a mixed-integer non-linear problem, which is challenging to solve. To address this challenge, a new algorithm is proposed, which iteratively places base stations, places IRSs, allocates resources, and adjusts phase shifts through an iterative process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using two different scenarios: one with a large number of base stations and small IRSs, and another with fewer base stations and larger IRSs. The results show that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of performance and complexity.

To improve the performance of binary in the data path, the branch prediction unit uses static and dynamic analysis to estimate branch outcomes. Deep learning has been employed in recent years to enhance branch prediction, leveraging its ability to model complex patterns and branch outcome distributions. This paper provides an in-depth review of deep learning-based branch prediction techniques, including static and dynamic approaches, as well as the challenges and opportunities in this field.

In robotics, active vision systems utilizing cameras, robots must precisely locate and track objects of interest. This research develops a novel active camera control method, utilizing a deep learning-based convolutional neural network that integrates an imitation learning framework. The proposed system leverages a deep neural network to map visual data to camera control signals, with the imitation framework enabling the training of the network by replicating the camera control actions of an experienced operator. The network is trained using a dataset of human operator inputs and visual data from a robotic head equipped with an RGB-D camera. The proposed system's efficacy is demonstrated through experiments involving robotic head tracking of moving objects in a simulated environment.

In this research, we investigate a non-linear, second-order difference equation derived from a discrete, two-dimensional Coulomb gas. This equation represents the free energy of a Coulomb gas confined within specific boundaries in the limit where N approaches infinity. To analyze this equation, we employ a methodical, iterative approach, and our primary finding is the equation's dependence on a single variable, which captures the essence of the gas's correlation function. This breakthrough has implications for understanding the properties of Gibbs measures in the Coulomb gas model.

We have developed a comprehensive model for the propagation of entangled photon pairs in non-absorbing media, taking into account the impact of all possible optical paths. This allowed us to analyze the spatial distribution of entangled photon pairs and their frequency correlation as they travel through a free space or fiber optic environment. Our findings show that the frequency correlation of the photons can be manipulated by adjusting the distance between the photons' emission points, the speed of light, or the characteristics of the optical medium. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that the frequency correlation of the photons can be used to measure the distance between the photons with high precision.

The study of strong coupling constants between vector mesons and light mesons using charmed and bottom mesons is conducted within the framework of QCD sum rules. The investigation yields robust results for the coupling constants, which are in agreement with those previously established in related studies. The findings suggest a similar pattern for the coupling constants associated with bottom mesons as compared to their charmed counterparts. The results also show that the coupling constants associated with bottom mesons are larger than those associated with charmed mesons.

This document is a chapter for the 2021 edition of the "Frontiers of Physics" journal, providing an overview of the near-term neutrino experiment landscape. It covers key aspects of the following neutrino experiments: Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE), Hyper-Kamiokande, MicroBooNE, NOvA, ORCA, PROSPECT, SBN, SHiP, the JUNO and ICARUS neutrino experiments at the Daya Bay site, as well as the Baksan Experiment with a Super-CDMS Detector (SuperCDMSD), the SNB experiment, the PTOLEMY experiment, the KATRIN experiment, the COHERENT experiment, the ORCA experiment, the J-PARC Neutrino Experiment, the T2K Experiment, the NOvA Experiment, the KBN experiment, the SHiP-HEMS experiment, the ORCA Experiment, the NOvA Experiment, the JUNO Experiment, the ICARUS Experiment, the Baksan Experiment, the Super-Kamiokande Experiment, the SNO+ Experiment, the SNB Experiment, the PTOLEMY Experiment, the KATRIN Experiment, the COHERENT Experiment, the J-PARC Neutrino Experiment, the KBN Experiment, the SHiP Experiment, the NOvA Experiment, the ICARUS Experiment, the JUNO Experiment, the Super-Kamiokande Experiment

In causal inference, linear regression is frequently used to identify the effect of a treatment on an outcome by adjusting for confounding variables. However, the weights assigned to treatment and control groups in linear regression models are often inconsistent and unreliable. Our research reveals that these weights can be viewed as a weighted least squares estimate, which can be computed quickly and efficiently. Our experiments demonstrate that this approach produces more accurate results than existing methods, including inverse probability weighting and double robust methods. Additionally, the weighted least squares approach can be easily extended to model complex relationships between variables and to handle multiple treatments and outcomes.

A novel model-free wide-area damping control approach utilizing voltage source converters is introduced, which enables these devices to provide stability services to the grid without needing to know the system model. The proposed strategy, which is suitable for synchronous machines, relies on a simplified model of the electrical network and does not require accurate knowledge of system parameters. The approach is further demonstrated to be robust against certain disturbances and reliable in the presence of parameter uncertainties. The proposed control scheme is evaluated through simulations on the IEEE 68-bus system, which show its effectiveness in damping oscillations.

We investigate the steady-state subradiance of two identical atoms in a non-interacting Dicke model. The model is characterized by a single, non-degenerate excited state and a threefold degenerate ground state, with each atom experiencing a collective decay into this state. The decay rate of each atom is determined by the number of excited atoms in the system. We derive an analytical expression for the subradiance rate of two atoms in the excited state, valid for any number of atoms. We find that this rate is significantly enhanced when the atoms are in the same state, and is inversely proportional to the number of atoms. We also observe that increasing the number of excited atoms leads to a decrease in subradiance, and that this behavior is sensitive to the number of atoms.

We are investigating the stability of a kink in the $\phi^4$-model, particularly where internal modes are present. Our analysis focuses on the stability under a distinct type of perturbation, specifically a non-standard one. Our findings indicate that the system remains stable for a certain range of wavenumbers in the fast variable. However, stability is lost when the wavenumbers become sufficiently large, leading to a non-standard type of instability. Our results differ from the conventional case and suggest that the system behaves like a kink with varying internal modes as the wavenumbers change.

The J-PARC hadron physics program includes three key experiments, E36, E47, and E48, which focus on studying the structure of hadrons. These experiments utilize high-energy proton and kaon beams, as well as various types of nuclear or particle detectors to achieve their goals. Specifically, E36, E47, and E48 aim to study the processes involving the production of vector mesons, vector meson decay, and meson-meson correlation. These studies are crucial for understanding the properties of hadrons and the strong interaction theory. Moreover, the experiments provide opportunities to investigate the phenomenon of color transparency, which can be observed through the study of vector meson production.

To address the issue of out-of-distribution shift in classification tasks, we propose a new method called Virtual Adversarial Discrete Disturbance (VADD) for consistency training. VADD aims to create a more robust classifier by introducing discrete disturbances that are tailored to the classifier's current state. These disturbances are designed to be virtually adversarial and effective in perturbing the classifier, making them particularly useful for testing classifier robustness. To achieve this, we utilize a conditional autoregressive model to generate the disturbances and a classifier to predict their effectiveness. The effectiveness of VADD is evaluated through experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 datasets, with VADD trained models exhibiting improved robustness against both white-box and black-box attacks.

Current methods for detecting polyps in endoscopic videos are limited by their failure to utilize the spatial-temporal information within consecutive frames effectively. This paper introduces a novel approach, multi-frame cooperation (MFC), which enables the use of features across multiple frames to improve detection accuracy. The proposed method includes a spatial-temporal transformation module that combines features from different frames and a cooperation cooperation module that enhances the representation of each frame by leveraging the results of the first module. The method is evaluated using the U-HAD dataset and outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall.

A novel sampling approach, known as Sequential Unequal Likelihood Sampling, or SULS, has been proposed for estimating the size of dynamic populations flowing through a fixed point. This method combines a priori knowledge of the population size with the results of past observations to determine the optimal space and time intervals for collecting the next batch of data. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that SULS is an optimal method for estimating the number of items in a stream, with its associated estimator following a normal distribution and achieving a minimum variance. The method's effectiveness is further demonstrated through a simulation-based evaluation.

The $^{57}$Zn nucleus undergoes $\beta$-delayed proton emission, which was previously predicted but not observed, and its study reveals a significant impact on the $rp$ process. The discovery of $^{57}$Zn's $\beta$-delayed proton emission, along with other findings, reveals a bypass in the $rp$ process, which significantly affects the $rp$ branching points. The new data, along with other experimental results, reveals a major impact on the $A=56$ $rp$ process hindrance point, which is a crucial factor in the $rp$ branching points. The new findings suggest a major impact on the $rp$ process, which is a crucial aspect of the $rp$ model.

Inspired by the number ring conjecture, we formulate a conjecture for number pencils, which are one-dimensional toroidal varieties with non-normal toric subvarieties analogous to those in toroidal embeddings. Our conjecture is proven for specific instances, including toric varieties with low complexity and smooth toric surfaces containing toric subvarieties with particular weights.

The connection between pulsars and high-energy gamma-ray emission has been well established, with gamma-ray sources being observed in nearly all classes of pulsars. The gamma-ray energy spectrum of pulsars typically peaks in the GeV range, while the GeV-TeV range reveals distinct features in the gamma-ray radiation patterns of pulsars. The TeV energy range, specifically, offers a unique opportunity to study the gamma-ray radiation mechanisms and the physical conditions in pulsars. The VERITAS array has conducted observations of 12 pulsars in the Northern Hemisphere, with the majority of these studies focused on the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) pulsars. The current research utilizes the entire available dataset from VERITAS, with the results presented for the first time in this work.

We examine the global existence and long-term behavior of solutions for a specific type of reaction-diffusion equation defined on irregularly shaped domains, with a nonlocal boundary condition. The nonlocal boundary condition is represented through a Fredholm operator that incorporates a singular weight function. The initial conditions and parameters of the equation are assumed to be sufficiently small. The nonlocal boundary condition and the singular weight function complicate the analysis, as they lead to a loss of regularity in the solution. However, we can overcome this issue by introducing a new variable and applying the contraction mapping principle. The resulting analysis reveals that the equation has a unique, globally existing solution that exhibits exponential decay in the interior of the domain, while the boundary variable exhibits polynomial growth. Furthermore, we can also establish the asymptotic convergence of the solution to a steady-state solution.

A novel, explainable machine learning method has been developed to identify and classify globular clusters and ultra-compact dwarfs within the Milky Way galaxy. This classification method leverages a combination of deep learning and convolutional neural networks to accurately distinguish between these two types of objects. By utilizing a dataset comprising 1,000 images of globular clusters and ultra-compact dwarfs, the trained model achieves an impressive 90% accuracy in identifying extragalactic globular clusters and ultra-compact dwarfs within the Hubble Space Telescope's F814W band. Furthermore, the model's ability to generate feature importance maps enables the visualization of key characteristics for each object type, thereby facilitating the analysis of their physical properties.

Online suggestion systems, crucial for e-commerce platforms, use machine learning algorithms to predict user preferences and provide personalized recommendations. These systems, however, are susceptible to errors resulting from incomplete or inaccurate data, making thorough testing under realistic conditions essential. We developed a simulation framework to evaluate online suggestion systems by generating synthetic user data, and our results show that simulations can effectively identify potential issues and distinguish between different algorithms. We found that simulations can detect differences in performance and help resolve real-world challenges faced by online suggestion systems.

This research paper focuses on developing a hypothesis test for a finite sample average when the underlying distribution is extremely skewed. The proposed test is applicable to a truncated sample average, where only a subset of the distribution is observable, and it relies on a small number of parameters for a large, heavily-tailed distribution. The test is robust and can function effectively even when the null hypothesis is false, and it maintains its power in a wide range of scenarios. The proposed test is also consistent, which means that it will eventually converge to a hypothesis that is true.

A cutting-edge approach to decoding motor imagery from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals involves using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). However, the effectiveness of CNNs in interpreting EEG signals is hindered by the inherent characteristics of these signals, such as non-stationarity and non-steady state behavior. To address this limitation, a novel CNN architecture based on the Sinc function is proposed. This architecture incorporates a Sinc-based filter layer, enabling the extraction of relevant features from EEG signals. The proposed model's performance was evaluated using a public dataset, and the results demonstrate the superiority of this approach over traditional CNNs in decoding motor imagery from EEG data.

In a two-dimensional anti-de Sitter space with noncommutative coordinates, we've developed a specific type of gauge theory that involves a particular algebra. This gauge theory is connected to a classical, commutative anti-de Sitter space with a unique feature. We've derived a set of rules that translate the algebraic structure of this noncommutative space into geometric terms, creating a correspondence between the noncommutative and classical spaces. This correspondence rule has a simple form and can be used to calculate various quantities in the noncommutative space.

The National Kidney Foundation estimates that approximately 100,000 individuals in the United States are waiting for a life-saving kidney transplant.  The primary obstacle is a shortage of available donor kidneys, which could be addressed by utilizing kidneys that are deemed unsuitable for their original recipients.  A 2017 study by the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine proposed a distribution-based allocation system, which would prioritize patients based on the length of time they have been waiting, but also suggested accepting unsuitable kidneys to minimize patient waiting times.  This study aims to mathematically model the decision-making process for accepting or declining a kidney that is considered unsuitable for its original recipient.  The goal is to maximize the probability that the recipient kidney is suitable for a patient, which would be the case if it was accepted by a patient with a shorter wait time than the original recipient, and then successfully transplanted into the recipient.  The study also considers the possibility of the patient being unable to tolerate the new kidney, which would result in the kidney being re-listed on the waiting list.  The study models the decision-making process as a two-stage Markov decision process and provides a computational algorithm to determine the optimal policy for accepting or declining the kidney.  The study also provides a simplified approximation of this policy, which can be easily implemented.  The results of the study show that the optimal policy and its approximation significantly outperform the conventional first-come-first-served policy in terms of

This paper presents two novel models, LSTM-D and HMM-D, which are derived from the combination of Hidden Markov Model and Long Short-Term Memory. The primary goal of these hybrid models is to improve the performance of the basic HMM and LSTM algorithms. The proposed models are evaluated using a dataset consisting of hand-written digits, and their accuracy is compared with the original HMM and LSTM algorithms. The results demonstrate that the hybrid models outperform their individual counterparts in terms of accuracy.

This paper introduces the generalized Volterra integral operator $V_\omega$ and establishes its boundedness in biased Bergman spaces for the exponential and modified Bessel weighted functions. We then derive the essential spectrum, spectrum, resolvent, and a Toeplitz operator on the range of $V_\omega$.

Large-scale NLP models are trained to perform multiple tasks, but their size hampers their practical use in industry due to high costs and environmental impact. We present a solution to this problem by developing a single model that can tackle various tasks across languages, reducing the need for multiple separate models. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this model in a real-world setting, where it outperforms individual task models in high-stakes customer feedback analysis. We also show that the combined model achieves comparable performance to individual task models when compressed using a shared set of parameters.

This paper explores data accessibility in the age of big data and artificial intelligence, highlighting the significance of open data in fostering innovation and economic growth. However, I argue that the current approach to making data available is inadequate, resulting in unintended consequences and the need for reevaluation. A shift towards a data market, as seen in other digital goods, could provide a viable alternative, but it would necessitate addressing the complexities involved. The paper concludes with my own experiences and perspectives on navigating the current data landscape as a researcher, student, and entrepreneur.

This paper presents a novel approach to constructing isogenies between the Jacobian varieties of hyperelliptic K3 surfaces. These isogenies are derived from a combination of maps defined on the surface's associated Weierstrass points, enabling the creation of a supersingular polarized K3 surface by applying this method to the Richelot isogeny of a supersingular elliptic curve. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates that the resulting K3 surface is essentially a decomposed version of the original Richelot isogeny. Additionally, the paper extends the method to the study of Howe curves and their properties.

Recent studies have shown that a small number of hot subdwarf stars exhibit strong magnetic fields. The presence of these fields in these stars is puzzling, as they should not have been able to sustain such strong magnetic fields given their mass and age. In this study, we identified three hot subdwarf stars, SDSS 143199.756639.713729, SDSS 150111.703.911.747, and SDSS 174718.754.787.551, through a search for magnetic fields in these stars using X-ray observations from the Chandra telescope. The magnetic field strength in these stars was found to be 1.5 million Gauss, 0.5 million Gauss, and 1.2 million Gauss respectively. The presence of these strong magnetic fields in these stars is likely the result of a binary merger event. The presence of these strong magnetic fields in these stars is also significant as it suggests that a binary merger event can create strong magnetic fields in these stars. The presence of these strong magnetic fields in these stars is also significant as it suggests that a binary merger event can create strong magnetic fields in these stars.

We investigate the problem of estimating a symmetric positive semi-definite matrix from an incomplete set of noisy measurements. The matrix in question can be expressed as the sum of a low-rank matrix and a matrix of lower rank. The available data only partially reveals the matrix's rank. The goal is to estimate the matrix using only a subset of its eigenvectors, which are assumed to be known. The estimation process involves two steps: first, we use these eigenvectors to project the matrix and eliminate the matrix of lower rank, and then we use a modified version of the Gaussian elimination algorithm to recover the matrix of interest. The effectiveness of this method is evaluated in terms of its ability to recover the matrix of interest. The results show that the method is capable of accurately estimating the matrix as long as the matrix of lower rank does not exceed a certain threshold. The method also exhibits robustness to noise and is faster than existing methods.

This paper presents WikiHist.html, a comprehensive HTML archive of the English Wikipedia's revision history, made available through a web service. By preserving the HTML formatting of each revision, WikiHist.html enables researchers to study and analyze the Wikipedia's evolution over time, offering insights into recent and long-term developments of this significant digital repository. As a substantial resource, WikiHist.html comprises 1.6 TB of data, with corresponding research endeavors, including data analysis, collaborative projects, and publications, such as exploring the evolution of Wikipedia's editing categories and constructing a Wikipedia history graph.

In a study of polar meron-antimeron lattices within twisted bilayers, we found that the interplay between the lattice structure and interlayer coupling leads to a variety of topological phases. The phase diagram reveals that the interlayer twist can induce either chiral or skyrmion-like textures in the interlayer coupling, which in turn result in either $Z_2$ or U(1) Chern insulators. The phase transition is characterized by a unique quantum critical point, where the system undergoes a transition from a single Kramers degeneracy to four degeneracies.

We have developed a theoretical framework for a non-flat universe that allows
for the existence of matter and cosmological vacuums as distinct sources of energy,
enabling the examination of both closed and open Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker
cosmological models. This framework accommodates a wide range of solutions to the
field equations, which can be explored through the use of a novel transformation
that maps any energy density to a standard matter density, thus facilitating a
unified analysis of diverse cosmological models.

The behavior of colloids near surfaces is significantly influenced by surface characteristics. In our study, we investigate how the periodic pattern of liquid crystals near surfaces affects colloid movement. We discovered that the surface patterns can steer colloids along specific paths, with their movement facilitated by the surface's periodic arrangement. Interestingly, the direction of their movement can be controlled by adjusting the surface pattern. This phenomenon allows for the creation of colloid pathways that can be manipulated for various applications.

The surface sensitivity of an asteroid's remote-sensing data is influenced by its shape, orientation, and the angle at which it meets the sunlight. This study examines the effect of the asteroid's shape on its reflectance spectra during a close planetary encounter. By analyzing the reflectance spectra of a large number of asteroids, we found that the shape of an irregularly shaped body has a significant impact on its reflectance. This impact is most pronounced when the asteroid's surface is at a 45-degree angle to the sunlight, resulting in the most informative spectra. Our findings suggest that the shape of an irregularly shaped asteroid can be determined by analyzing the reflectance spectra during a close planetary encounter, even when the asteroid's surface orientation is unknown.

Molecular machines rely on conformational transitions, which are notoriously difficult to capture in simulations. To study these transitions, we developed a new method that combines a quantum computer with a sampling approach. This method allows us to target unusual transitions, such as those that don't occur frequently. We applied our technique to the molecular rotor Regio A, and found that it successfully identified the Regio A rotor's rare conformational shifts. This breakthrough is significant because it paves the way for using quantum computers to investigate regioselectivity in molecular machines.

The Monte-Carlo code MAPPIES was developed to simulate inverse external Compton scattering in complex systems involving relativistic beams and non-relativistic photon fields. The code accounts for the polarization of relativistic particles and photon fields, allowing it to model a variety of scenarios, including the interaction of relativistic jets with their own magnetic fields. In this paper, the underlying physics of MAPPIES is explained, along with the methodology used to implement the polarization effects of relativistic particles and photon fields. The code's performance is demonstrated through a comparison with laboratory experiments and a case study of the interaction between a relativistic jet and a toroidal magnetic field. The polarization effects are found to significantly influence the emission spectrum, particularly in scenarios involving high levels of polarization.

Utilizing data from satellite measurements, satellite-based atmospheric reanalysis, and satellite-derived wind speed data, we have developed a mathematical model to simulate the distribution of Arctic sea ice thickness across different regions. This model accounts for the influence of various factors, including the ice's vertical and horizontal movements, collisions, and the effects of wind and water pressure. We found that the model accurately replicates the observed distribution of sea ice thickness in the Arctic, and that the inclusion of collisions and wind and water pressure effects is crucial to this accuracy. We also discovered that the model's sensitivity to the parameters governing collisions and wind and water pressure effects is dependent on the ice thickness. This model provides a more comprehensive representation of Arctic sea ice dynamics than previous models, and can be applied to other studies of sea ice in the Arctic.
We analyze the generalized Weierstrass semigroup at specific points on certain maximal curves and determine the specific points of order two on these curves.

This study offers a comprehensive overview of deep learning-based singing voice synthesis systems. It begins with an examination of the defining characteristics of singing voice and the challenges of creating authentic synthetic singing voices. The study then delves into the evolution of singing voice synthesis technology, highlighting the pivotal role of deep learning methods. The focus is then shifted to the most effective neural network models that have contributed to the advancement of singing voice synthesis. The study also explores the practical applications of synthesized singing voices, including the use of virtual idols and automated music production tools. Finally, it identifies key issues that need to be addressed in order to further improve the state-of-the-art in singing voice synthesis technology.

The bird sound dataset, NIPS4Bplus, comprises over 20,000 audio recordings of more than 2,000 bird species, offering detailed metadata and expert annotations.  Originally developed from the BirdCLEF4 challenge, NIPS4Bplus has undergone significant updates to its metadata and audio content.  This paper delves into the dataset's updates and its applications in tasks such as bird species identification through audio examples, bird habitat and species mapping from acoustic data, and bird sound classification based on metadata.  The paper also presents the outcomes of the BirdCLEF2020 challenge, BirdCLEF2021, and BirdCLEF2022, which utilized the NIPS4Bplus dataset in various tasks.  The dataset is accessible through the OpenBIRDS platform.

Time-of-Flight (TOF) event cameras, capable of capturing frame-free, event-based data, have gained popularity in recent years due to their potential for low-latency and power efficiency. However, event-based data often requires adjustment to accurately represent real-world scenes, a process that can be challenging for inexperienced users. This tutorial aims to guide newcomers through the process of correcting their event data to achieve accurate results in various applications.

Graph analysis has become a fundamental tool in handling and examining large datasets. The diverse range of graph algorithms and techniques available today has created a complex and overwhelming environment for researchers and practitioners. This survey aims to provide an in-depth review of graph analysis, starting with its history and core components. We delve into the categories of graph data, algorithms, and systems, as well as essential techniques such as graph summarization, visualization, and clustering. We also discuss recent advancements in graph neural networks and their applications in supervised learning and graph generation. Additionally, we explore innovative graph analysis applications and discuss the future of graph analysis research.

We provide a compact formal representation of the exceptional set for the
Hodge conjecture in codimension 2 abelian varieties, which was first
identified by de dios. This exceptional set is a union of countable projective
subvarieties, and we have established that the exceptional set for abelian
surfaces is a finite union of uniruled subvarieties.

A precise and efficient approach to retinal surgery is crucial for successful outcomes. However, the delicate nature of the surgical site and limited visibility due to vitreous opacity can make it challenging for surgeons to accurately navigate. To address this issue, we've developed a novel solution that utilizes a lightweight, rigid endoscope and a lightweight, elastic light source to create a precise, three-dimensional model of the surgical site. By combining this model with real-time tracking data from the light source and endoscope, our system enables surgeons to accurately position instruments and achieve successful outcomes in simulated experiments.

This note provides two novel equations for $F$-polynomials, which are involved in 
deformation quantization and are characterized as elements in a quotient of the 
symmetric group algebra corresponding to the symmetric group $S_n$.

The widespread use of passwords for authentication has been a major source of security vulnerabilities, prompting the development of alternative solutions. Notably, FIDO2, a new authentication method, has gained significant attention, but its effectiveness is still a topic of debate. This paper assesses the current state of FIDO2, highlighting its advantages and limitations, and examines its potential to replace traditional password-based authentication for online applications.

We apply the Weyl-Wigner formalism to lattice models, specifically the Ising model, within a compact discrete space, and demonstrate that its phase transition can be identified through a singular four-dimensional representation of the space in the momentum space. This representation, tied to the lattice's periodic symmetries, exhibits a phase transition where it transitions from being almost completely degenerate in the paramagnetic phase to developing a dense set of non-degenerate eigenvalues in the ferromagnetic phase.

Our research focuses on how various design elements of YouTube, such as recommended content and playlist organization, influence users' sense of agency over their video consumption. We developed a tool to measure the impact of different design choices on user control and developed a set of experiments to test these design elements. The results of our study indicate that certain design elements, such as autoplay, and other features like "Watch Next," erode users' sense of agency, whereas other features like playlists and search functions enhance it.

Its behavioural equivalence, $=$, is defined based on the ability of processes to transform one another. A behavioural equivalence is considered complete if it can be used to prove process equivalences established by other equivalences. A key result in this study shows that the $\pi$-Calculus' $=$ equivalence is complete with respect to two other equivalences, $(=$>$)$\sim$($\nu$)$=$($\sim$)$\sim$($\nu$)$=$($\sim$)$\sim$ and $(=$>$)$\sim$($\sim$)$=$($\sim$)$($\sim$)$=$($\sim$)$, which are based on the ability of processes to communicate and the absence of non-trivial processes. A new, efficient algorithm is proposed to generate a gray code sequence for a specific class of structured trees, yielding a concise, easily verifiable formula that highlights the underlying structural characteristics of these trees.

The ACTS algorithm is now incorporated into the Jupyter Notebooks utilized by sPHENIX track reconstruction performers for candidates reconstructed by the sPHENEX and sPHinx frameworks. ACTS calculates the four-track vertex likelihood for each track and the four-track vertex distance for tracks in events where four tracks are identified as a $4\pi$ four-particle decay of a $\Lambda_c$. It then utilizes these values to determine the 4-track vertex position and the four-track distance between vertices. ACTS is applied to events where four tracks are identified as a $\Lambda_c$ by the sPHenix track reconstruction algorithm.

This research introduces a new approach for computing the discontinuity term in the space-time Finite Element Method (FEM). The approach is based on the quadrature by element (QbE) method, which is integrated with a novel extension for space-time discretization. This extension enables the computation of the discontinuity term in terms of the average values of the fields, thereby maintaining consistency with the underlying weak form. The proposed method is applicable to arbitrary temporal interpolation functions and has been validated through numerical experiments.

A specific type of signed graph known as a signed graph, defined by assigning either + or - to the edges of a standard graph, has been studied in this context. A uni-directed signed graph, which always moves in one direction, is considered and the conditions under which these graphs can create closed loops, or circular flows, have been identified. The discovery that every standard graph can be represented as a uni-directed signed graph with circular flows has also been made.

The modular subset sum problem is a classic problem in computer science that challenges given positive integers $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ and integers $0<q<1<Q$, with the goal of finding a subset $I$ that maximizes the value of $\sum_{i\in I} w_i\pmod q$ modulo $q$, but not modulo $Q$. This problem has significant applications in machine learning and statistics, particularly in a specific regime where $q$ is much smaller than $Q$, and $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ are randomly distributed, where we present a deterministic algorithm that achieves a significant improvement in this regime, with the running time of $O(n\log n)$ and space complexity of $O(n)$. This algorithm is a first deterministic algorithm that achieves a significant improvement in this regime, with the running time of $O(n\log n)$ and space complexity of $O(n)$.
